trip.title: Switzerland
assumptions: Every traveller holds a Swiss Half Fare Card (CHF 150 each, valid one calendar month, bought to cover 4-13 September).
Flights are booked. Four land at Zurich on Friday 4 September at 20:30, the fifth on Saturday 5 September at 06:30, and all five leave for Tel Aviv on Sunday 13 September at 11:45.

Four things are booked and fixed: the first night at the Zleep Hotel in Kloten, the Historical apartment in Schwyz for 5-7 September, LaVida Peak at Reichenbach im Kandertal for 7-11 September, and the van - a 7-seat VW Caddy from Europcar, collected at 22:00 on Friday 4 September and returned Friday 11 September at 12:00, seven days at ILS 1,505, about CHF 414.

The base for the mountain days is the Kandertal, not Grindelwald. Grindelwald sold out for these dates and nothing in the village matched LaVida Peak, so the fallback became the plan. It costs about 75 minutes each way to Grindelwald Terminal on Jungfraujoch morning - and it buys Oeschinensee at 23 minutes, Blausee at 16 and the Niesen at 10, none of which were reachable from Grindelwald at all.

One figure in the whole plan is still a guess: the CHF 20 placeholder for parking at the Zleep on the 4th. The Zleep room itself came in at ILS 962. Everything else is a published 2026 tariff, a booked rate, or a live quote read on 24 August 2026.

Fares are the operators' published 2026 tariffs, verified in August 2026 against Jungfraubahnen, Schilthornbahn, Rigi Bahnen, SGV, Aareschlucht AG, Oeschinensee AG and the Titlis and Niesen operators.
At five people a 7-seat MPV works: the back row folds flat for the luggage. At six it would not have.

The shekel figures convert at CHF 1 = ILS 3.94, which is what the card was actually charged for the Half Fare Cards on 24 August - the market rate that day was 3.73, so the difference is the card's own foreign-currency fee. The euro figures convert at the market rate, 1.068, because nothing on this trip is paid in euros. Always ask to be charged in Swiss francs rather than shekels at a Swiss card terminal: choosing shekels hands the exchange rate to the merchant and it is always worse.

trip_wide_costs.note: Bought on 24 August 2026, and valid from 4 September for one calendar month. It halves almost every fare in this plan, and on the Niesen and the Engstligenalp it beats the senior tariff outright.

Booked with Europcar at ILS 1,505. Collected at 22:00 on Friday the 4th, straight off the flight, and returned Friday the 11th at noon. Rentals bill in 24-hour blocks, so a Friday-night collection and a Friday-noon return is still seven days and the same money - but confirm the rate did not move when the pick-up did.

trip_wide_costs.item: Fuel, approx 670 km, plus the top-up before the airport
trip_wide_costs.note: The Kandertal base adds about 145 km across the block, almost all of it on Jungfraujoch morning. The hire is full to full - refuel in Kloten town on the last morning, never at a motorway services.

trip_wide_costs.item: Food beyond the two big shops
trip_wide_costs.note: Self-catered breakfasts and lunches, four dinners out for five at Swiss restaurant prices. Parking at Weggis, Lungern, Lauterbrunnen and Grindelwald Terminal is costed on its own day; LaVida Peak has free parking on the premises.

days.title: Land at Zurich, sleep in Kloten
days.movement: Land at 20:30, four of the five. Passport control and bags, then through to the Rental Centre on Level 1 of the Airport Center - the van is booked for 22:00 - and three kilometres up the road to the hotel in Kloten, in the room by about half past ten. Taking the van tonight rather than on Saturday morning costs nothing extra and saves the whole 07:15-to-09:00 wait tomorrow.

group.item: Zleep Hotel Kloten, rooms for four

tips: Only four beds are needed tonight. The fifth traveller lands at 06:30 tomorrow morning.
Zurich is one hour behind Tel Aviv in September, so there is no jet lag to fight - only the flights themselves.
The Zleep night was billed at ILS 962, which is the CHF 244 here. The CHF 20 for parking is still a placeholder - it is the only guess left in the whole plan.
One of the four who land tonight has to be the named driver, and it is a five-minute drive at ten at night after a flight. Short, but agree who is doing it before you are standing at the desk.
Check what the hotel charges to park - it is CHF 20 here as a placeholder, and airport hotels vary from free to CHF 25 a night.

days.title: Meet the early flight, cross to Zug, and settle in Schwyz
days.sleep: Schwyz (the Historical apartment, night 1 of 2, booked)
days.movement: Back to the terminal for the 06:30 arrival - allow until about 07:15 for passport control and bags. The van is already yours, so you leave straight from the kerb: the A4 south past the Zugersee, Zug for late morning, Schwyz by about half twelve. Check-in is 16:00 by key box, so the afternoon belongs to Brunnen, five minutes down the road.
days.on_foot: Zug's lakefront and old town are flat, paved and full of benches, and the Zytturm is better looked at than climbed - though it is there if anyone wants the roofs and the lake from the top. Then the promenade at Brunnen, where the lake turns the corner into the Urnersee and the mountains close in on both sides, and a swim off the lido for whoever fancies it: the water is still warm in the first week of September.
tips: Do the big shop TODAY. Tomorrow is Sunday and Swiss supermarkets shut - the Coop and Migros in Schwyz close around 17:00 on a Saturday and do not open again until Monday.
Because the van came last night, there is no 09:00 rental desk to wait for. That is nearly two hours back on the first proper morning - enough for a real breakfast in Zug rather than a hurried one.
Zug's Kirschtorte is the real thing here, not a tourist confection - the Speck bakery on Alpenstrasse invented it in 1915.
Brunnen is five minutes from the apartment, and the view down the Urnersee from the quay is the one on all the old posters. Go at the end of the afternoon, when the light comes down the lake.
Do not take the van into Zug's old town. Use the Postplatz or Casino garages and walk in - it is pedestrianised anyway.

days.title: Mount Rigi from Weggis, and Lucerne at dusk
days.sleep: Schwyz (the Historical apartment, night 2 of 2, booked)
days.movement: Drive round the lake to Weggis, about half an hour, and park at the pier. Cable car up to Rigi Kaltbad, then the cog railway to Rigi Kulm. Come down the same way, or walk the 4 km from Kulm to Kaltbad. The van waits at the pier all day, so the late afternoon is the boat across to Lucerne and the 19:12 back.
days.on_foot: Cable car and cog railway to the summit, the flat panorama terrace and the restaurant at the top. There is no walking in this day at all unless you want it - and if you do, Rigi Kulm down to Kaltbad is 4 km and about an hour and a quarter on a wide easy track with the whole of Lake Lucerne underneath you the entire way, while everyone else rides down and meets you there. In Lucerne the Chapel Bridge, the waterfront and the Old Town squares are all level, and the Musegg Wall towers are stairs for whoever wants them.
tips: The last boat back from Lucerne leaves at 19:12 and reaches Weggis at 19:53. Miss it and it is train plus bus, 51 minutes, CHF 5.20 - not a disaster, but the van is at the pier and the boat is the nicer end to the day.
See the Chapel Bridge in the early evening rather than at midday. That is what this day is shaped around.
Rigi Kulm is 1,798 m and the terrace is exposed. Take a layer even if Weggis is warm.
Weggis parking is CHF 13 for 24 hours and it is not free, whatever the village website implies.
If Rigi is in cloud, do not go up. Take the boat down to Flüelen instead and the train back - three hours through the dramatic far end of the lake, all of it seated.
Everything is shut today except restaurants and the stations. This is the whole reason the big shop happened yesterday.

days.title: Over the Brünig to the Kandertal, by way of Lungern and the Aare Gorge
days.sleep: Reichenbach im Kandertal (LaVida Peak, night 1 of 4, booked)
days.movement: Schwyz to Lucerne on the A4, then the A2 and A8 south through Sarnen and Giswil. Stop at Lungern for the lake and, if the morning is clear, the Turren cable car. Over the Brünig, then fifteen minutes off the road at Meiringen for the Aare Gorge. On through Brienz and Interlaken, along the Thunersee to Spiez, and south into the Kandertal. About 150 km and two and a half hours of driving, four and a half door to door with both stops.
days.on_foot: The lakeside path at Lungern-Obsee is flat and paved with a restaurant at each end, and the Turren cable car is ten minutes up to a terrace facing the Bernese Alps across the water. At the gorge, go in from the WEST entrance: the first half, as far as the middle, is level, railed and passable with a wheelchair or a narrow pushchair, and the operator calls it the most beautiful part anyway. Carrying on to the east end makes it the full 1.4 km, about 45 minutes.

per_person.item: Lungern-Turren cable car return, half fare

tips: The Aare Gorge is CHF 13 a head in 2026, not the CHF 10 that half the internet still quotes. Parking at the West entrance is free and takes a van.
Both gorge entrances stay open until 18:30 through 20 September, after which it drops to 17:30. There is plenty of margin for a mid-afternoon arrival.

Do NOT pull into the Chälrütirank viewpoint above Lungern with a seven-seater. It is an unmarked pull-in on a wide bend with a handful of spaces and coaches fill it. Use the Obsee car park instead - 222 spaces, CHF 5 for 24 hours.
The A8 Soliwald tunnel at Brienzwiler, right on this route, is closed every night from 20:00 to 05:00 until 18 September. Be over the Brünig before eight and it is irrelevant.
The Turren cable car runs every 20 minutes and the last one DOWN on a weekday is 17:00. Do it in the morning or not at all.
The Half Fare Card buys nothing at the Aare Gorge - it is an attraction, not a transport tariff. It does halve the Turren, to CHF 18 return.
Frutigen is three minutes from the apartment and has the last big Coop before the valley narrows. Worth knowing on the way in, because Reichenbach itself is small.

days.title: Jungfraujoch - Top of Europe
days.movement: The long morning. Out of the door at 06:40 for the 08:00 first gondola: down the Kandertal to Spiez, the A8 along the Thunersee, Interlaken, Wilderswil, Zweilütschinen and up to Grindelwald Terminal - 46 km and about 75 minutes in a van. Then the Eiger Express to Eigergletscher, 15 minutes, and the cog railway through the inside of the Eiger to Jungfraujoch, about 25 more.
days.on_foot: Sphinx observation deck by lift - never the stairs - then the Plateau and the Ice Palace. Everything up there is indoors, level and lift-served, and ninety minutes to two hours is plenty at this height. Whoever wants the walk gets off at Eigergletscher on the way down for the Eiger Trail to Alpiglen: 6.5 km, about two and a half hours, almost all of it descending along the foot of the north face, with a train back from Alpiglen.

per_person.item: Jungfraujoch return from Grindelwald Terminal, half fare

tips: THE SEAT RESERVATION IS MANDATORY from 1 May to 31 October, so it applies today. CHF 10 a head, booked with the ticket at top-of-travel.jungfrau.ch. Without one the railway can simply be full. Be through the turnstiles ten minutes before departure.
THIS DAY FLOATS. Check the summit webcams at breakfast and go on the clearest morning of the four. Nothing else in the plan is ruined by cloud and nothing else costs this much.
Do NOT buy the Good Morning Ticket. It starts at CHF 190.40, it does not combine with a Half Fare Card, and it forces you off the summit by 13:17. The plain half-fare ticket is cheaper.

3,454 m, and the Sphinx deck is 3,571 m. About half of adults get a headache, dizziness or no appetite up here, usually two to twelve hours in - which is exactly why a short visit is the plan. Move slowly, drink water, skip the alcohol, take the lift.
September averages a high of 1 C and a low of minus 5 C at the top, before the wind. Coats, hats, gloves, sunglasses and sunscreen - the glare off the snow is worse than the cold.
The last half-hour of the ascent is inside a tunnel with no view at all. That is normal, not a fault.

Anyone with a heart or lung condition, sleep apnoea, or medication for either should ask their doctor before the trip rather than on the platform. There is a staffed medical room with oxygen at the top.

Blausee is sixteen minutes from the apartment and open late. After five hours at 3,454 m that is a far better evening than another climb - a flat 300 m asphalt path to the water and the glass-bottomed boat included in the entry.

days.title: Schilthorn and Piz Gloria, then dinner on the Niesen
days.movement: Drive to Lauterbrunnen, 38 minutes, and park at the station. Ask for tariff D, the Rundreise via Grütschalp: funicular up the cliff, the shelf train along to Mürren, cable car through Birg to the summit, and back down the other side through Stechelberg. In the evening, the Niesen funicular from Mülenen - ten minutes from the apartment, and Wednesday is one of its two evening nights.
days.on_foot: The shelf train from Grütschalp to Mürren is the loveliest flat ride in the Oberland - twenty minutes of Jungfrau across the valley with nothing asked of you - and Piz Gloria turns a full circle while you eat. The Thrill Walk at Birg is a catwalk bolted to the cliff face with open metal grating underfoot and the Skyline Walk is out on the summit terrace: both are optional and both are easy to walk past. The Niesen in the evening is thirty seated minutes to 2,362 m and a restaurant at the top.

per_person.item: Schilthorn round trip via Grütschalp, half fare
Niesen return from Mülenen, half fare

tips: The Schilthornbahn rebuild is FINISHED - the last of the new cars was inaugurated on 2 April 2026 and there are no closures on these dates. This is the opposite of the Titlis situation.

Ask for tariff D. The circular route via Grütschalp and Mürren costs CHF 115 full and CHF 57.50 on a Half Fare Card - identical to the plain out-and-back - so there is no financial reason to do the same valley twice.
The last car off the summit is 17:50, reaching Mürren at 18:05. The last train Mürren to Lauterbrunnen is 19:58.
The Piz Gloria brunch needs a table reservation. It is not a walk-up.

Lauterbrunnen's multi-storey is CHF 18 for the day and connects straight to the station. Neither the operator nor the garage publishes a height limit, so measure the van before committing to it - Stechelberg, at CHF 7 for eight hours, is open-air with no limit at all.

The Niesen runs evening services on Wednesdays and Fridays only, from 1 July to 28 October, with ascents 17:30-19:30 and the last descents at 23:25. Wednesday the 9th is the one evening of this trip it is possible - Friday the 11th you are already at the airport. Book the summit restaurant; these evenings sell out.

Brunch at 2,970 m and dinner at 2,362 m in one day is a lot of mountain. If it is too much, make Piz Gloria a coffee and keep the Niesen - it is ten minutes from bed and the Half Fare Card halves it to CHF 32.
The Thrill Walk floor is see-through. Some people find that far more unnerving than they expect, and there is no shame in taking the inside route.

days.title: Oeschinensee, and Blausee on the way home
days.movement: The short day, and deliberately so. Twenty-three minutes up the valley to the Oeschinen gondola at Kandersteg, then the gondola, and from the mountain station either a twenty-minute path down to the lake or the electric taxi. Blausee sits between Kandersteg and home, so it costs nothing to stop there on the way back. Thirty-six kilometres in total.
days.on_foot: Trail C, the Direttissima, is a wide gravel and part-asphalt path, twenty to twenty-five minutes down to the shore and explicitly stroller-suitable - but it is a 100 m climb coming back, so take the electric shuttle up rather than earn it twice. At the lake there are rowing boats, a 750 m summer toboggan run and the shore circuit under the Blüemlisalp walls. At Blausee the path from the gate to the water is 300 m of flat asphalt and the glass-bottomed boat is in the entry price; the woodland paths behind it, Felsenzimmer and the Wolfsschlucht, are roots and soft earth and are the part of it worth doing.

per_person.item: Oeschinensee round trip including the ascent time slot, half fare

group.item: Lunch at the Oeschinensee lakeside restaurant

tips: THE ASCENT TIME SLOT IS MANDATORY from 20 June to 20 September, and two of the five slots for 10 September are ALREADY SOLD OUT - 11:30-13:00 and 13:00-14:30 both show zero. The other three each showed over 200 places on 24 August.

TAKE THE 10:00-11:30 SLOT, not the earliest one. The electric taxi from the mountain station down to the lake does not start until 10:45, and the alternative is a twenty-five minute path with a 100 m climb back. Going up at 08:30 means waiting at the top station for the better part of two hours.

One ticket covers everything: the round trip INCLUDES the ascent slot and the descent. The operator's words are that the descent can be made at any time during operating hours - and within the next seven days if you stay up there. CHF 22.50 a head on the Half Fare Card against CHF 40 full. There are NO staffed ticket counters at the valley station, so buy it online; the machines hold only a small remainder.

The cable car is step-free the whole way to the mountain station. From there the electric taxi runs to the lakeside restaurant and back every half hour, first departure 10:45 from the top, last 17:30 from the lake, paid on the spot. Capacity is limited and only one wheelchair travels per trip, but guests with limited mobility have priority.
If the day has to move, the time slot can be rebooked free of charge.
Trail B, the Huble mountain path, is CLOSED for construction. Take trail C, which is the stroller-friendly one anyway.

Blausee is open daily and the Half Fare Card buys nothing there - it is an attraction, not a transport tariff. Booking a table at the restaurant refunds half the admission at lunchtime and all of it in the evening.
This is the softest day of the trip on purpose. It sits between Jungfraujoch and the airport run, and after nine days five people need one.

days.title: Down the Kandertal and back to Zurich
days.sleep: Kloten (Hotel Welcome Inn, a triple and a double, night 1 of 2)
days.movement: Out of the Kandertal to Spiez, the A6 through Thun to Bern, then the A1 east to Zurich. About 170 km and two hours, all of it motorway. Van back at the airport by 12:00, refuelled. Then the hotel, and the afternoon is free.
days.on_foot: A quiet afternoon. The train from the airport into the city is 13 minutes, and the lake promenade and Bahnhofstrasse ask nothing of anybody. Beyond that, the old town, the Lindenhof terrace, and a swim off one of the lake badis if the weather has held.

group.item: Hotel Welcome Inn, Kloten - a triple and a double, night 1 of 2

tips: THE VAN IS DUE BACK AT 12:00. The hire runs seven 24-hour blocks from 22:00 on Friday the 4th, and an hour late can bill as a whole extra day. Leave the Kandertal by 09:00 and there is an hour in hand.

The Jodelfest opens in Grindelwald today and takes the village over - over a thousand performers and no visitor parking. Being in the Kandertal instead means none of it is your problem, and this is the one day the base pays you back.
Refuel in Kloten town, not at the airport and never at a motorway services. The hire is full to full and the services charge the worst prices in the country.

The Welcome Inn splits five across two rooms: a triple at 18 m2 with two singles and a sofa bed, and a double, each with its own bathroom. CHF 655 for the pair non-refundable, or CHF 771 with free cancellation to 14:00 on arrival day and nothing to pay until 9 September. Scored 8.5 from 1,514 reviews, and the airport shuttle is free - which is the point on Sunday, when you need the terminal by 08:45.
Nothing is booked for this afternoon on purpose. After four mountain days in a row, an empty half-day in a flat city is not a gap in the plan.

Drop the bags at the hotel BEFORE returning the van, not after. The hotel is five minutes from the terminal, the van is due back at noon, and carrying four days of luggage onto a bus is a waste of a perfectly good vehicle.

days.title: Zurich on foot, and the Knabenschiessen
days.movement: No van and no driving - it went back yesterday. The train from the airport into the city takes 13 minutes and runs every few minutes. The old town on foot all day, and the evening at Albisgütli.
days.on_foot: Lindenhof for the view over the roofs, the Fraumünster windows and the lake promenade - all flat and paved, with somewhere to sit every hundred metres. The Grossmünster tower and the lanes behind Niederdorf are there for whoever has the legs for them. At the Knabenschiessen: a funfair, food stalls and most of the city out on level ground. Leave whenever you like, or stay - it runs to 01:30 and the trains keep going well past midnight.

group.item: Hotel Welcome Inn, Kloten - a triple and a double, night 2 of 2

tips: The Knabenschiessen is Zurich's own festival, 12 to 14 September, and today is the opening day. Free to walk into, and it runs until 01:30.
Tram 13 normally terminates at Albisgütli, but during the festival it stops at Laubegg, four minutes short. There is no visitor parking at all - which is one more reason the van went back yesterday.
Pack tonight, properly. Tomorrow's terminal time is 08:45 and it is not negotiable.
The shops inside Zurich main station open on Sundays, which almost nothing else in Switzerland does - useful if anything has been forgotten.
If the festival is too much after nine days, the lake boats run into the evening and the Old Town does not need a ticket.

days.title: Late morning flight home
days.movement: The hotel shuttle to the terminal. No van to return - it went back on Friday.
tips: Be at the terminal by 08:45 for the 11:45 departure. Flights to Tel Aviv carry extra security interviews and Zurich asks three hours for them rather than the usual two.
Check-in opens at 04:00 at the earliest, so there is nothing to gain by arriving before those three hours.

weather_swaps.do: Move the day. It is the only thing here that weather ruins outright and the most expensive ticket on the trip, and it is why the Tuesday floats across the whole Grindelwald block.
Boat down to Flüelen and back by train. Three hours through the dramatic far end of Lake Lucerne, all of it seated, none of it weather-dependent.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A spare mountain day, or a washed-out one
weather_swaps.do: Grindelwald First. The Cliff Walk is free with the gondola and Bachalpsee is 3 km each way on a wide, gently rising path. It is 75 minutes away from this base, which is why it is here rather than in the plan.

Trümmelbach Falls. Ten glacier falls carved inside the mountain, reached by a lift built into the rock - but stairs beyond the halfway point and permanently wet underfoot, so anyone unsure of their footing should stop at the middle.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A wet morning in the Oberland
weather_swaps.do: Schynige Platte. A vintage cog railway from Wilderswil, a free alpine garden with over 750 species at the top, and noticeably fewer people than the famous peaks.
Harder Kulm. Ten minutes by funicular from Interlaken Ost, flat at the top, the classic two-lakes view - and it runs to 21:10 in September, so it fits after a mountain day rather than instead of one.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A morning that wants a waterfall
weather_swaps.do: The Engstligenalp cable car above Adelboden. The upper fall passes directly beneath the cabin, so it is a 600 m waterfall seen with no walking at all, and there is a viewing platform at the valley station too. Runs to 18 October, 08:30-17:00.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A flat afternoon off the mountains
weather_swaps.do: Thun. Twenty-five minutes down the valley: a medieval castle above a river town, arcaded streets with the shops up on the roofs of the arcades, and the lake at the bottom. No cable car, no altitude, no tickets.
Männlichen. Gondola up from Grindelwald Terminal and the cog railway down from Kleine Scheidegg, with the almost level Panoramaweg between them - the gentlest high ridge walk in the region.

booking_order.note: Booked. The figure here is still the estimate rather than the confirmation, and so is the CHF 20 for parking that night - replace both when the email arrives.
Booked. Key box from 16:00 on the Saturday, so the afternoon belongs to Brunnen.

booking_order.item: LaVida Peak, Reichenbach im Kandertal - 7 to 11 September
booking_order.note: Booked, and flexible. This is the base for all four mountain days, and it is the reason Oeschinensee, Blausee and the Niesen are in the plan at all.
Booked at ILS 1,505. Collected at 22:00 on Friday the 4th and back Friday the 11th at noon: still seven 24-hour blocks, and it deletes the wait for the rental desk on Saturday morning.

booking_order.item: Hotel Welcome Inn, Kloten - a triple and a double, 11 to 13 September
booking_order.note: Two rooms rather than one big one: a triple, 18 m2 with two singles and a sofa bed, and a double. CHF 655 for the pair non-refundable, or CHF 771 on the rates that cancel free until 14:00 on the day of check-in with nothing payable until 9 September - and that is the rate carried here, because it costs nothing today and still lets you change your mind on the morning. Scored 8.5 from 1,514 reviews, a kilometre out, free airport shuttle, which is what matters for an 08:45 terminal time on the Sunday. The one-room alternative is the Allegra Lodge family room at CHF 605 flexible - CHF 166 cheaper, but 40 m2 for five with a shared bathroom. Zleep for these two nights needs three doubles and comes to CHF 1,034.

booking_order.item: Oeschinensee round trip with the ascent slot, five, Thursday 10 September
booking_order.note: One purchase, not two: under TICKETS OESCHINENSEE take "Round trip with the cable car incl. time slot for the ascent", pick 10 September, the GA / Half Fare price of CHF 22.50, and quantity five. The slot is mandatory to 20 September - no slot, no boarding, even with a valid ticket - but the descent is free of it and can be made any time the cable car is running, which is 08:30 to 18:00. Take 10:00-11:30 rather than the earliest slot, because the electric taxi down to the lake does not start until 10:45. Rebooking the slot is free.

booking_order.item: Five Swiss Half Fare Cards, covering 4 to 13 September
booking_order.note: Bought on 24 August 2026. The one purchase on this list that made the trip cheaper rather than dearer: CHF 733 of full fares each becomes CHF 405. Not buying them costs the party CHF 890. Take the visitor card - one calendar month, CHF 150 - and not SBB's own CHF 190 Half Fare Travelcard, which is an annual product for residents and a different thing entirely.

booking_order.item: Jungfraujoch return from Grindelwald Terminal, five, with the mandatory seat reservations
booking_order.note: The reservation is CHF 10 a head, compulsory from 1 May to 31 October, and it is what actually gets you on the train. Book once the week's forecast is readable - the Tuesday floats across the whole Kandertal block, so move the day rather than spend this much in cloud. Skip the Good Morning Ticket: it does not stack with the Half Fare Card and it forces you back down by 13:17.

booking_order.item: Piz Gloria brunch, five, Wednesday 9 September
booking_order.note: The table reservation is required, not optional. It is also the easiest CHF 190 to save on this whole trip - the restaurant turns its full circle whether you order brunch or a coffee.

Evening services run Wednesdays and Fridays only, and on Friday the 11th you are already back at the airport - so it is that Wednesday or not at all. The CHF 160 is the five rides; dinner is on top. Reserve by telephone on +41 33 676 77 11.
Bought at the Weggis valley station on the morning. Nothing sells out.

booking_order.item: Boat, Weggis to Lucerne and back, five
booking_order.note: At the pier. If the Rigi is in cloud this becomes the day instead: Flüelen and back is three seated hours through the dramatic end of the lake.

booking_order.item: Schilthorn round trip, tariff D via Grütschalp, five
booking_order.note: Ask for tariff D by name at the window. It covers the descent you actually plan and costs the same CHF 57.50 on the Half Fare Card as the plain Stechelberg return.
At the valley station. The first thing to drop if the Monday morning runs late.
CHF 13 a head, not the CHF 10 still quoted all over the internet. Go in from the West entrance: free parking, and the level half.
At the gate. The glass-bottomed boat is included in the entry price.
In the SBB app or at any machine, on the Half Fare Card. Buy them on the day you use them, not before.
Free to walk into, and Zurich's old town needs no ticket at all. Tram 13 terminates at Laubegg during the festival, four minutes' walk. There is no visitor parking, so leave the van at the hotel.

totals.note_vs_six: At six the shared costs barely move - LaVida Peak, the van and the rooms at each end cost much the same either way - so the total would rise by about one more person's tickets and food while the figure each fell. Five costs less overall but more each. At six the luggage would not have fitted in the Caddy.

savings.note: Nine nights in the most expensive country in Europe, and most of the money is already booked or already spent. What is genuinely still open is small, and this is the whole of it: what can go, what dropping it actually costs you, and the four lines that look like savings and are the opposite.

cut.instead: Have a coffee at the revolving table instead. You are already paying CHF 287 to be up there, and the view does not know what you ordered.

cut.item: Lunch at the Oeschinensee lakeside restaurant
cut.instead: Carry a picnic down Trail C. There will be a fridge full of the second supermarket shop, and the lake is the point rather than the kitchen.
Ten minutes to a terrace, on a day that already has the Brünig, the Obsee and the gorge in it. The first thing to go if the morning runs late anyway.

cut.item: Two of the four dinners out, cooked at the apartment instead
cut.instead: Dinner for five at Swiss restaurant prices runs CHF 250 to CHF 350 a time. LaVida Peak has a kitchen and you will have shopped twice by then. Keep two nights out and make them the two you will actually remember.

keep.why: Cutting these does not save CHF 750, it costs CHF 890. Every fare in this plan is already priced at the half fare.
Ten minutes from the door, CHF 32 a head, and the evening service runs on Wednesdays and Fridays only - one of which you spend flying home. The cheapest distinctive thing the Kandertal buys you.
CHF 10 a head against a CHF 598 ticket, and without them the ticket does not board.

keep.item: The Oeschinensee round trip and its slot
keep.why: The slot is mandatory to 20 September and two of the five for the 10th have already gone. It is inside the ticket, so there is nothing here to cut anyway - and there are no staffed counters at the valley station.
